chapter: Earl Hines, Chicago and later gigs
title: Ray Nance persuades him to join Lunceford
summary: Ray Nance urged him to go, saying he would get a better shot, and saw him off at the train.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: How was it that Ray convinced you to make the change?
Well, I wasn't going, so Ray said I would go if I were you. He says because you get a better shot at things, which I did. You know, I'm glad he did. In fact,

Ray went to the -- Stanley Dance said he wrote that in a story. Ray went out to the station. I had to catch a train ride, oh man to New York. I hate to think about it now. A coach (Laughter) -- I was so tired when I got into New York.

But we had -- I know we had a little half a pint of liquor, and we went out to 63rd and Stony. Ray went out with me late at night to catch this late train at night -- riding into New York. But Ray walked out -- came out to the station with me.
